newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent holds steady line with little momentum.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent holds steady line with little momentum.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures traded sideways over the morning on a steady one or two cents either side of Thursday's $18.21 close. Traders said there was little buying or selling momentum to push the market either way.
By 1230 GMT the August Brent contract was pegged one cent lower at $18.20 a barrel with $18.18 trendline support intact.
Brokers said Thursday's fall in Brent was mainly the result of profit-taking, although news that Iraqi crude exports were a step closer to resumption was also a factor.
Most brokers expect levels to move up rather than down today with a bigger rise on Monday if the market can close above support.
However, analysts said that a breach of $19 on Monday would be more difficult after Thursday's losses created some strong resistance.

GNI Research said in their daily report, "The failure of front month Brent to break above the downtrend creates a very powerful line of resistance for the future with three well spaced points of contact (between the June 9 high of $24.90, May 16's $20.60 high and Wednesday's $18.96 high). The short term uptrend line (from June 20's $17.48 low) clearly acted as support on Thursday, but is nowhere near as strong as it's negative brother".

However, despite the short-term bearishness technical indicators continue to point to room for a further upside to most markets. RSIs across the IPE and NYMEX remain in neutral territory but momentum indicators remain bullish with trendline supports in place on both crude and products.

Gas oil stood 75 cents down at $163.75 a tonne stuck in a narrow 50 cent range and looking likely to struggle to get back above trendline support by the close with high ARA stocks and thin demand from the key German market pressuring spot prices.
